svg.title: Radiation & half-life
svg.desc: Alpha, beta, gamma: Alpha: helium nucleus, highly ionising, stopped by paper/skin; cm in air. Beta: fast nuclear electron; medium ionisation, stopped by mm of aluminium; metres in air. Gamma: EM radiation; less ionising, very penetrating; thick lead/concrete reduces intensity. Random decay: Cannot predict when one nucleus will decay. A large sample follows a predictable pattern. Activity = decays/s (Bq). Count rate is detector events per unit time; not all emissions are detected. Half-life: Same time interval halves the remaining undecayed nuclei or activity. 640 → 320 → 160 → 80 Bq: three half-lives. With 2 h half-life, elapsed time = 6 h. Remaining vs decayed: After n half-lives, remaining fraction = (½)ⁿ. Three half-lives: remaining 1/8, decline 7/8. Remaining : initial = 1:8; decline : initial = 7:8. Background correction: Measure background without source; subtract from total using matching time units. 84 total − 4 background = 80 counts/s source. One half-life later: 40 + 4 = 44 total. Graph & measurement: Read time between a source count and half that count; check other starting values. Keep geometry/shielding fixed. Longer counting and repeats reduce random fluctuations; they do not control decay.
